claims.text: Adaptive bias force or metadynamics can substantially reduce the cost of obtaining fusion properties for high-entropy systems.
Adaptive bias force or metadynamics can substantially reduce the cost of obtaining high-temperature thermodynamic properties for high-entropy systems.
The proposed advanced-sampling calculations can maintain accuracy while reducing computational cost.
The intervention is to incorporate adaptive bias force or metadynamics into free-energy calculations.
The proposed free-energy calculations retain vibrational entropy.
The proposed free-energy calculations retain anharmonic effects.
The proposed free-energy calculations retain electron–vibration coupling.
Increased sampling efficiency causes faster convergence of free-energy calculations.
Faster free-energy convergence reduces computational cost relative to explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics workflows and TOR-TILD.
The reduced computational cost will not cause a significant loss of accuracy in predicted fusion properties.
The reduced computational cost will not cause a significant loss of accuracy in predicted high-temperature thermodynamic properties.
The method is applicable to multicomponent high-entropy systems.
The method is applicable under high-temperature conditions relevant to fusion.
The magnitude of cost reduction and retained accuracy may depend on the high-entropy system and sampling technique.
Failure to obtain at least a twofold computational-cost reduction while remaining within 5% of baseline predictions would falsify the hypothesis.
